title: Shift CI to immutable hybrid bases and experimental cache priming
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Background: Our CI images have diverged into many ad-hoc bases and long-lived mutable containers. This increases build flakiness, slows developer iteration, and leaks ephemeral state between runs. Goal: Replace the largest friction sources by introducing a small set of immutable hybrid base images (minimal runtime + optional language shims), and an experimental cache-priming step that seeds frequently used layer artifacts and package caches to improve first-time build latency. Out of scope: full migration of legacy language runners (we will gate them behind opt-in sub-issues).
acceptance_criteria: Introduce 3 immutable hybrid base images (node, python, go) documented in infra/docker/README.md
CI jobs that used previous mutable bases must be reproducible on immutable bases with no change to test semantics
Average cold-build latency for core monorepo target reduced by >=30% on the primary CI pool
Layer-level cache hit rate increases to >=80% for warm runs in the experimental pool
Provide migration guide and a feature flag to opt pipelines into the new bases
No increased flakiness observed in the 2-week canary window (error rate delta < 0.5%)
tasks: Design immutable base image spec and baking process (sha-pin runtime components)
Implement hybrid shims that install language toolchains at build-time but keep base small
Add optional 'cache-priming' job that pre-populates CAS and package caches in a dedicated pool
Update core CI pipeline templates to support 'base-image' variable and feature flag
Run phased canary: 10% pipelines -> 50% -> full after 2-week stability window
Instrument build latency and cache-hit metrics on console and add dashboards
notes: Decision: prefer immutable images + build-time shims over large multi-language fat bases to reduce CVE surface and image churn
We will sign all published base images and publish SBOMs alongside each tag
Priming approach: weekly cron job that builds representative targets at known commit hashes and pushes layers to distributed CAS
Fallback: if a job fails on immutable base, runners will revert to the previous mutable builder for that pipeline until triage completes
Storage impact: priming increases CAS size by ~12GB in experimental pool; we have budgeted for this in infra quota
